Admin.vendorAccessHelp: Per vendor or rental company. “Vendor” = the Vendor tag: planners can add the vendor to a project, where it sees the materials, 2D map, timetable and run-down read-only. “Vendor stock” = the tables & chairs it rents out (not the team’s regular stock, My stock); only with it on does the login get the Planner ⇄ Vendor switch and the Vendor page. Switching off only hides; nothing is deleted, and ticking again restores it.
Admin.makeVendorHelp: Creates the vendor company and links it to the planner’s own login: same email and password, with a switch between Planner and Vendor. The vendor gets what a rental company has (rentable tables and chairs) plus the team’s stock, shared with My stock. Afterwards, use “Vendor access” above to switch the Vendor tag or Vendor stock on and off.
Admin.makeAVendorAlsoAPlanner: Make a vendor also a planner
Admin.makePlannerHelp: Gives an existing vendor login a planner account too (its own team of one, as manager), so the same login can switch between Planner and Vendor and add vendors to its own projects.
Admin.doneThatLoginIsNowAlsoAPlanner: Done. That login is now also a planner.

Rsvp.mapHelp: Optional. The venue and each hotel are placed on the map from their Google Maps link, or from their address when there is no link. There is nothing to pin by hand. Guests can tap a hotel on the map to see its details, open it in Google Maps or visit its website. The map appears in the hotels section of the page; hotels you have switched off there are left off the map too.
Rsvp.mapVenueAddressHelp: Used when the venue's map link (under Details) can't be read, or when there is no link.
Rsvp.mapVenueFound: The venue is on the map.
Rsvp.mapVenueMissing: The venue could not be found on the map. Check the map link under Details, or add an address here.

Rsvp.mapHotelNotFoundSaved: {name} was saved, but it could not be found on the map. Check its Google Maps link or address.
Rsvp.mapLookupUnreachable: The map lookup service could not be reached just now. Your changes are saved; save again in a moment to place it on the map.
Rsvp.translateIntro: Text you write here (welcome note, schedule, dress code, area text, captions, hotel descriptions and booking notes) is translated into Spanish, English and French automatically when you save, so guests see it in the language they choose. Names and addresses stay as written. Check the result with Preview page, switching the language at the top.
Rsvp.translateFailed: Saved, but the translation could not be made just now. Guests will see this text as you wrote it, in every language, until you save again.
Rsvp.translateNotConfigured: Saved. Automatic translation is not set up on this site yet, so guests see this text as you wrote it, in every language.
Rsvp.dayByDayHelp: Optional. One entry per moment of the weekend, shown on the page like a programme: day and time on the left, title and place in the middle, description and a short label (for example the dress code) on the right. They are ordered by day and time.
Rsvp.translateDone: Everything is translated. Open Preview page and switch the language to check it.

WhatsNew.title: What’s new in Venuria
WhatsNew.subtitle: Changes since you were last here

Tour.notice: Couldn’t set up a practice project, so the tour skips the project pages.
Tour.chooseMode: Choose seated or standing to continue the tour.
Tour.offerBody: Take a short guided tour of the main pages. You can replay it any time from Settings.
Tour.errNoPlanner: No planner account linked to this login.
Tour.errNoVenue: No venue with a room is set up yet, so there is nothing to practise on.
Tour.errSample: Could not create the sample project.
Tour.welcomeBody: A short tour. Use this menu to move between Projects, Stock, Team and Settings; “Last project” returns you to the page you were last on. Esc stops the tour, and you can replay it from Settings.
Tour.newProjectBody: Pick the venue, the couple’s names and the event date. New projects are Public: your team can view them, but only people assigned to a project can edit it. You can also create Private projects, which only assigned people can view. Every project visible to you is listed below.
Tour.hubBody: Everything for one event: the editor, summary, payments and documents, timetable, run-down list and guest list.
Tour.hubSample: This is a practice project we created for you, “Alex & Sam (sample)”. You can delete it at any time from the bottom of this page. The hub holds everything for one event: the editor, summary, payments and documents, timetable, run-down list and guest list.
Tour.placeTableBody: Click and drag anywhere on the map to move around it; scroll or pinch to zoom. Drag a table from the catalogue onto the floor plan, then choose how many chairs it gets.
Tour.placeTableDo: Click and drag anywhere on the map to move around it; scroll or pinch to zoom. Try it out: drag a table from the Tables section onto the floor plan, then choose how many chairs it gets.
Tour.placeTableDone: That’s how a layout is built. Tables can’t be placed outside the room’s border or over fixed objects. These restrictions are created and modified by the venue. You can change the chair count later. We’ll go over more details next.
Tour.canvasBody: Click a table to select it. A panel on the right shows its rotation and chairs. Drag a table to move it, or Ctrl + left-click and drag to select several objects. Sizes and availability come from the venue and rental catalogues.
Tour.roomsCapacityBody: Switch between the venue’s rooms and areas. Each area has its own guest limit, set by the venue, for Standing or Seated use. Choose how an area will be used to see how many people it holds.
Tour.autoArrangeBody: Fills the room with dining tables, avoiding the room’s border, fixed objects and anything already placed. Nothing existing is moved or deleted.
Tour.seatingZonesBody: Turn on the seating plan to seat guests. Click a chair to assign someone, or drag them from the guest list on the right of your screen. Use Zones to mark areas such as a dance floor. Auto-Arrange keeps tables out of them.
Tour.exportBody: Download the room as a JPG, or open the Summary for a list of everything placed, stock shortfalls and a PDF export of that list.
Tour.addGuestsBody: Add guests one at a time, or upload a file with a list of guests. Select a guest to link family members and add dietary needs, hotel details and more.
Tour.addGuestsDo: Try it out: type a guest’s name and press “Add guest”. You can also upload a file with a list of guests.
Tour.addGuestsDone: Added. Select a guest to link family members and add dietary needs, hotel details and more.
Tour.rsvpBody: Share one link with all your guests so they can answer themselves. Answers appear automatically in your list, and new names are flagged “To review”.
Tour.paymentsBody: Log each deposit, instalment and balance with its due date. Reminders start 7 days before a payment falls due. You can also add contracts and quotes, and use “Update” on each one to keep track of its versions.
Tour.timetableBody: Plan the day hour by hour, across several days if needed, and tag blocks with the vendor responsible.
Tour.timetableSample: An example day, so you can see how it looks. Plan the day hour by hour, across several days if needed, and tag blocks with the vendor responsible.
Tour.rundownBody: Your timetable also appears here as a list for the team and vendors. It’s easier to read, and you can print it or save it as a PDF.
Tour.rundownSample: The same example day appears here as a list for the team and vendors. It’s easier to read, and you can print it or save it as a PDF.
Tour.stockBody: Your catalogue, purchases and sales, with average cost and margins. Managers and leads can edit it. Members can view it and add sales. You can also add one-time orders to keep track of them.
Tour.teamBody: Invite colleagues with a one-time link so they can create their own account. Members see public projects and the ones assigned to them. Leads see and can assign every project.
Tour.settingsBody: Your name, password and company details live here too. You can also change the style of your PDFs from here before you download them. Replay this tour any time with this button.

ProjectVendors.title: Vendors on this project
ProjectVendors.help: Vendors you add can look at this project, read-only: the materials, the 2D map, the timetable and the run-down. They never see guests, payments or documents. They also appear in your vendor list for the timetable and run-down, with the contact details they entered. Vendors without a Venuria account are added there with “+ New vendor”.
